source_caption:
In a matter of seconds, Kendall Roy goes from wildly unhinged to cold corporate killer.

The brilliance of Succession’s opening is perfectly captured in the first few minutes when Kendall Roy shifts from blast-singing rap music in the back of a town car to stepping out as a cold, hyper-focused corporate heir. The sudden drop of Nicholas Britell’s iconic theme music acts as an immediate tonal anchor, signaling the exact moment the "unhinged" mask slips away to reveal the crushing, serious weight of the Roy empire.

It is arguably one of the greatest openings in television history. By blending grainy, nostalgic 8mm home videos of a toxic elite childhood with the jarring, high-stakes reality of modern corporate warfare, the sequence establishes a perfect visual metaphor for generational trauma and the hollow pursuit of legacy.

source_details.synopsis: Succession is an American satirical comedy-drama television series created by English screenwriter Jesse Armstrong that aired for four seasons on HBO from June 3, 2018, to May 28, 2023. The series centers on the Roy family, the owners of global media and entertainment conglomerate Waystar RoyCo, and their fight for control of the company amidst uncertainty about the health of the family's patriarch. Brian Cox portrays the family patriarch Logan Roy. His children are played by Alan Ruck as Connor, Jeremy Strong as Kendall, Kieran Culkin as Roman, and Sarah Snook as Shiv.
